To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the probability of the 7→ 1 unique second-forbidden transition in 137Cs to be (8.7±2.0)×10−4% and the intensity of the 5→1 E5 transition to be < 1×10−4%.
The intensity of the unique forbidden β transition of 137Cs was measured and found to correspond to log f2 = 16.4±0.1.

1) the unique second-for forbidden transition in the decay of Cs137 has been measured and the probability of its decay has been determined; 2) the technique for determining the value of log f2 unt in calculations of the transition matrix elements has been discussed and the possible intensity of the E5 transition in the decay chain Cs137 has been estimated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for unique second-forbidden transitions in the decay of nuclei with A = 127–129, 131, 137, 139.
the search for the second-forbidden β decay of 137Xe.
the study of unique second-forbidden beta transitions in 137Cs and the possible existence of the unique second forbidden beta transition in the decay of the 129I ground state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 7/1+ → 1 /2+ transition in 129Xe (129I) is not forbidden.
the unique second-for-fobidden β decay of 137 Cs is established.
the 129I decay is unique in the sense that it does not have any allowed β transitions, and the only possible β transitions are unique first- or second-forbidden transitions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the unique second-forbidded β transitions of the 7→5 and 7→1 types are not observed.
the unique second-forbiddent β transitions are much less probable than the allowed β transitions.
the unique second-forbiden β transitions are not so rare as previously supposed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the unique second-for forbidden transition is the dominant process in the decay of the ground state of the 137Cs nucleus.
the unique second-for forbidden β transition is not a rare process.
